cases.sentence: Зачем египтянам давать повод говорить: «Он вывел их со ___, чтобы убить в горах и стереть с лица земли?» Оставь Свой пылающий гнев, смягчись, не наводи на Свой народ беду.
cases.explain: «злым умыслом» — after the preposition «со», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Why should the Egyptians talk, saying, ‘He brought them out for evil, to kill them in the mountains, and to consume them from the surface of the earth?’ Turn from your fierce wrath, and turn away from this evil against your people.

cases.sentence: Моисей повернулся и сошел с горы с двумя ___ свидетельства в руках.
cases.explain: «каменными плитками» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Moses turned, and went down from the mountain, with the two tablets of the covenant in his hand; tablets that were written on both their sides. They were written on one side and on the other.

cases.sentence: Когда Иисус услышал гул ___, он сказал Моисею:
cases.explain: «кричащего народа» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: When Joshua heard the noise of the people as they shouted, he said to Moses, “There is the noise of war in the camp.”

cases.sentence: Он бросил ___, которые нес, разбив их на куски у подножия горы.
cases.explain: «каменные плитки» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: As soon as he came near to the camp, he saw the calf and the dancing. Then Moses’ anger grew hot, and he threw the tablets out of his hands, and broke them beneath the mountain.

cases.sentence: Тогда я сказал им: «У кого есть ___, пусть снимет их».
cases.explain: «золотые украшения» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: I said to them, ‘Whoever has any gold, let them take it off.’ So they gave it to me; and I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf.”

cases.explain: «другой день» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: On the next day, Moses said to the people, “You have sinned a great sin. Now I will go up to Yahweh. Perhaps I shall make atonement for your sin.”
